rv.q: You would not know it from a slowly brilliant first act, stupendously performed by its cast, which mixes fact with fiction in its dramatisation of a scandalous moment in the life of the children’s writer Roald Dahl.
Famously, he didn’t play nicely. But even so, it’s a shock to see John Lithgow’s towering performance capture all of this storied author’s cruelties in Mark Rosenblatt’s debut play.
